backtracking__n-queens-n-queens-ii.title: N-Queens / N-Queens II
backtracking__n-queens-n-queens-ii.statement: Place `n` non-attacking queens on an `n x n` chessboard so that no two queens share a row, column, or diagonal. **N-Queens** returns all distinct board configurations (each row a string of `.` and `Q`); **N-Queens II** returns just the number of distinct solutions.

examples.explanation: There are two placements of 4 queens on a 4x4 board.

approaches.name: Row-by-row backtracking with occupancy arrays
approaches.idea: Place exactly one queen per row. A cell `(r,c)` is safe iff column `c`, main diagonal `r+c`, and anti-diagonal `r-c+n-1` are all unused. Mark the three arrays, recurse to the next row, then unmark. When row `n` is reached a full valid board has been built. This turns each conflict check into O(1).

approaches.name: N-Queens II count with bitmasks
approaches.idea: When only the count is needed, represent used columns and the two diagonals as bits of three integers. At each row the free positions are `~(col|diag|anti) & fullMask`; iterate over set bits with `p & -p`. Shifting the diagonal masks left/right when recursing propagates the attack lines. This is the fastest practical way to count.
approaches.time: O(n!) but with tiny constant per node

backtracking__n-queens-n-queens-ii.insight: One queen per row; check column and both diagonals in O(1) via three occupancy sets (bitmasks for pure counting).

backtracking__sudoku-solver.title: Sudoku Solver
backtracking__sudoku-solver.statement: Fill a partially completed `9 x 9` Sudoku board (empty cells are `'.'`) so that every row, every column, and each of the nine `3 x 3` sub-boxes contains the digits `1-9` exactly once. Modify the board in place; a unique solution is guaranteed.

examples.input: board with 51 filled cells (standard LeetCode example)
examples.output: the same board with every '.' replaced by the correct digit
examples.explanation: Each row, column and 3x3 box ends up holding 1-9 once.

constraints: It is guaranteed that the input board has exactly one solution

approaches.name: Backtracking with O(1) validity via boolean masks
approaches.idea: Precompute `rows[i][d]`, `cols[j][d]`, `boxes[b][d]` marking whether digit `d` already appears in row `i`, column `j`, or box `b = (i/3)*3 + j/3`. Scan cells in row-major order; for each empty cell try every digit not conflicting in its three masks, set the masks, recurse to the next cell, and undo on failure. Returning `true` up the stack stops as soon as the board is complete.

backtracking__sudoku-solver.insight: Keep three boolean masks (row, column, box) so each digit-legality test is O(1); backtrack cell by cell in row-major order.

backtracking__word-search-ii.title: Word Search II
backtracking__word-search-ii.statement: Given an `m x n` grid of characters and a list of `words`, return all words from the list that can be formed by a path of horizontally or vertically adjacent cells, where each cell is used at most once per word.

examples.explanation: "oath" and "eat" trace valid adjacent paths; "pea" and "rain" do not.

constraints: board[i][j] and words[i] consist of lowercase English letters

approaches.name: Build a trie of the words, then DFS each cell once
approaches.idea: Insert all words into a trie so that a single grid traversal can test every word simultaneously; each node stores the full word at its end. DFS from every cell following trie edges: if the current letter has no child the branch is dead, pruning early. When a node holds a word, add it and null it out to avoid duplicates. Mark visited cells with `'#'` and restore on backtrack.
approaches.time: O(m*n*4*3^(L-1)) where L is max word length
approaches.space: O(total letters in words) for the trie

backtracking__word-search-ii.insight: Put the dictionary in a trie so one DFS tests all words at once and dead prefixes prune the search immediately.

backtracking__palindrome-partitioning-ii.title: Palindrome Partitioning II
backtracking__palindrome-partitioning-ii.statement: Given a string `s`, partition it so that every substring of the partition is a palindrome. Return the **minimum number of cuts** needed.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters only

approaches.name: Precompute palindrome table, then 1-D cut DP
approaches.idea: Pure backtracking is exponential, so use DP. First build `pal[i][j]` = is `s[i..j]` a palindrome, filling `i` from right to left so `pal[i+1][j-1]` is ready. Then `dp[j]` = min cuts for prefix `s[0..j]`: if `s[0..j]` is itself a palindrome `dp[j]=0`, else `dp[j] = min over i of dp[i-1]+1` for every `i` where `s[i..j]` is a palindrome. Answer is `dp[n-1]`.

backtracking__palindrome-partitioning-ii.insight: Precompute an O(n^2) palindrome table, then dp[j] = min(dp[i-1]+1) over palindromic suffixes s[i..j].

backtracking__permutations-ii-subsets-ii.title: Permutations II / Subsets II / Combination Sum II
backtracking__permutations-ii-subsets-ii.statement: Three duplicate-handling backtracking classics on an array that may contain repeats. **Permutations II**: all unique permutations. **Subsets II**: all unique subsets (the power set). **Combination Sum II**: all unique combinations that sum to `target`, each number used at most once.

examples.explanation: Each element used once; no duplicate combinations.

approaches.name: Sort, then skip equal siblings at the same depth
approaches.idea: Sort the array so equal values are adjacent. The universal duplicate rule: at a given recursion level, skip a value equal to its predecessor when that predecessor was not chosen for this branch. For subsets/combinations use a `start` index and skip `i>start && a[i]==a[i-1]`; for permutations use a `used[]` flag and skip `i>0 && a[i]==a[i-1] && !used[i-1]`. Combination Sum II also breaks when `a[i] > target` (sorted prune).
approaches.time: Permutations O(n*n!), Subsets O(n*2^n), CombSum2 O(2^n) worst case

backtracking__permutations-ii-subsets-ii.insight: Sort first; skip a duplicate at the same tree level (start-index rule for subsets/combos, !used[i-1] rule for permutations).

backtracking__expression-add-operators.title: Expression Add Operators
backtracking__expression-add-operators.pattern: DFS over digit splits carrying running value and last operand
backtracking__expression-add-operators.statement: Given a string `num` of digits and an integer `target`, insert the binary operators `+`, `-`, `*` (and nothing else, no unary) between digits so the resulting expression evaluates to `target`. Return all such expressions. Operands may span multiple digits but must not have leading zeros.

approaches.name: DFS choosing the next operand and operator, tracking multiplication
approaches.idea: At each position pick the next operand `num[pos..i]` (breaking if it has a leading zero). For the first operand just seed the value. Otherwise branch on `+`, `-`, `*`. Multiplication needs the previous operand: undo its additive contribution and re-add it multiplied, i.e. `eval - prev + prev*cur`, and carry `prev*cur` as the new `prev`. Use `long` to avoid overflow while accumulating.
approaches.time: O(4^n) expressions (n operator gaps, ~4 choices each)

backtracking__expression-add-operators.insight: Carry both the running total and the last operand; for '*' correct the total with eval - prev + prev*cur and set prev = prev*cur.

backtracking__remove-invalid-parentheses.title: Remove Invalid Parentheses
backtracking__remove-invalid-parentheses.pattern: Compute minimum removals, then DFS removing exactly that many
backtracking__remove-invalid-parentheses.statement: Given a string `s` containing letters and parentheses, remove the minimum number of invalid parentheses to make the string valid. Return all distinct valid strings achievable with that minimum number of removals.

examples.explanation: Removing one ')' yields these two valid strings.

constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters and parentheses '(' and ')'
There will be at most 20 parentheses in s

approaches.name: Count surplus '(' and ')', DFS removing exactly those counts
approaches.idea: First pass computes how many '(' (`rmL`) and ')' (`rmR`) must be deleted to reach validity. DFS scans from a moving `start` index and, to avoid duplicate results, only removes the first bracket of a run of identical characters. Remove a ')' only while `rmR>0` and a '(' only while `rmL>0`. When both counters hit zero, validate the remaining string and collect it.
approaches.time: O(2^n) worst case over bracket positions

backtracking__remove-invalid-parentheses.insight: Pre-count the minimum '(' and ')' to delete, then DFS removing exactly those, skipping duplicate characters in a run to dedupe results.

backtracking__partition-to-k-equal-sum-s.title: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets
backtracking__partition-to-k-equal-sum-s.statement: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, determine whether it is possible to divide the array into `k` non-empty subsets all having equal sum.
constraints: The frequency of each element is in the range [1, 4]

approaches.name: Fill one bucket to target at a time, largest-first, with pruning
approaches.idea: If the total is not divisible by `k`, or the max element exceeds `target = sum/k`, it is impossible. Sort ascending and fill from the largest element downward. Recursively fill the current bucket to `target`; when it reaches `target`, start a fresh bucket. Key prunes: skip used items and any that overflow the bucket; if the first item placed into an empty bucket leads to failure, the whole configuration is impossible (return false); skip equal values already tried at this level.
approaches.space: O(n) for the used array and recursion

backtracking__partition-to-k-equal-sum-s.insight: Fill buckets one at a time to sum/k, largest element first; if the first element of an empty bucket can't be placed successfully, it's impossible.

backtracking__letter-combinations-restor.title: Letter Combinations / Restore IP Addresses
backtracking__letter-combinations-restor.pattern: Position-indexed DFS building the string incrementally
backtracking__letter-combinations-restor.statement: Two incremental-construction backtracking problems. **Letter Combinations**: given digits `2-9`, return all letter strings the number could spell on a phone keypad. **Restore IP Addresses**: given a digit string, return every valid IPv4 address formable by inserting three dots (each of the 4 parts is 0-255 with no leading zeros).

examples.explanation: Two ways to split into four valid octets.

approaches.name: DFS by position; append a choice, recurse, backtrack
approaches.idea: Letter Combinations: map each digit to its letters and recurse over positions, appending one letter per digit to a shared StringBuilder and undoing on return. Restore IP Addresses: try segment lengths 1-3 at each cut; reject a segment with a leading zero (length>1) or value >255, and since larger lengths only get bigger/keep the leading zero, `break` on failure. After placing 4 parts, accept only if the whole string was consumed.
approaches.time: Letters O(4^n * n); IP O(1) (bounded constant search)

backtracking__letter-combinations-restor.insight: Recurse by position, append one choice and undo it; for IP addresses cap at 4 parts, reject leading zeros / >255, and require the string to be fully consumed.

backtracking__matchsticks-to-square.title: Matchsticks to Square
backtracking__matchsticks-to-square.statement: Given an array `matchsticks` where `matchsticks[i]` is a stick length, decide whether all sticks can be used (each exactly once, none broken) to form the four sides of a square.

examples.explanation: Total 16 -> side 4, but a stick of length 3 can never complete a side of 4 with the remaining sticks.

approaches.name: Fill 4 buckets to side = total/4, largest-first backtracking
approaches.idea: This is the k=4 case of equal-sum-subset partition. If the total is not divisible by 4, or fewer than 4 sticks, or the longest stick exceeds `side = total/4`, return false. Sort ascending and place sticks largest-first into buckets; complete one bucket to `side` before starting the next. Prune: skip used or overflowing sticks, abort the whole search if the first stick of an empty bucket fails, and skip duplicate lengths at a level.
approaches.time: O(4^n) worst case with heavy pruning

backtracking__matchsticks-to-square.insight: It's Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets with k=4: fill four side-length buckets largest-first with the same pruning.
